note: Derived from specs/** by the compiler. Do not edit; edit the spec and rebuild.

approve.human.cancel.title: Cancel Approval Request
approve.human.cancel.summary: Compensation for approve.human.request. Withdraws a pending request when the run is abandoned upstream, so a reviewer is never asked to approve something that no longer exists.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

approve.human.request.title: Request Human Approval
approve.human.request.summary: Renders a preview, sends it to the reviewer's surface, and waits on a resumable webhook. An unanswered approval EXPIRES into the parked state — silence is never consent, and a timeout must never fall through into a post.

asset.ledger.append.title: Append to Run Ledger
asset.ledger.append.summary: One row per produced or published artefact in a human-readable sheet, plus the machine telemetry row. The original workflows logged to Sheets ad hoc with different columns each time; a single schema here is what makes a cross-estate dashboard possible at all.

asset.store.delete.title: Delete Stored Asset
asset.store.delete.summary: Compensation for asset.store.put. Removes the object and tombstones the DAM row rather than hard-deleting it — an orphaned row is recoverable, a lost audit trail is not.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

asset.store.put.title: Store Asset Durably
asset.store.put.summary: Copies a provider URL or binary into tenant-scoped durable storage, computes a checksum for dedupe, embeds it for semantic search, and registers it in the DAM. Every producing capability ends here — that single rule is what turns scattered generations into a compounding asset library.

copy.localize.title: Localise Copy
copy.localize.summary: Adapts copy into a target locale — not translation: currency, date format, idiom, proof conventions and the locale's own compliance variant. Separated from generation so a locale can be added without regenerating source copy.

copy.longform.generate.title: Generate Long-form Copy
copy.longform.generate.summary: Blog posts, articles, case studies, PDP copy, email sequences, one-pagers. Structure comes from the brief and the vertical profile, never from a hard-coded template inside the workflow.

copy.script.generate.title: Generate Video Script
copy.script.generate.summary: A shot-by-shot script whose beat structure comes from the vertical's `shot_grammar`. This is the mechanism that makes one video factory produce a UGC unboxing for DTC, a before/after for a plumber and an annotated mechanism walkthrough for an equipment maker — same workflow, different grammar.

copy.short.generate.title: Generate Short-form Copy
copy.short.generate.summary: Social posts, captions, headlines, subject lines, ad variants, CTAs. Produces N variants in one call because variant count is the lever that makes paid testing and channel fan-out affordable.

dist.publish.blog.title: Publish to Blog / CMS
dist.publish.blog.summary: Owned-channel adapter. Publishes as a draft by default and requires an explicit flag to go live — owned properties carry SEO consequences that outlive the campaign.

dist.publish.email.title: Publish to Email
dist.publish.email.summary: Owned-list adapter. The highest-consequence organic channel in the estate: an email cannot be unsent, reaches an audience that gave permission, and a mistake costs deliverability that takes months to rebuild. Always approval-gated, always suppression-checked.

dist.publish.linkedin.title: Publish to LinkedIn
dist.publish.linkedin.summary: Channel adapter with asset registration, first-comment support and scheduling. Compensable: a post can be deleted, so this one declares a compensation capability and the orchestrator can roll it back if a sibling step fails hard.

dist.publish.telegram.title: Publish to Telegram
dist.publish.telegram.summary: Channel adapter. Consumes a channel-neutral PublishRequest and speaks Telegram. Re-verifies its own gates rather than trusting the caller — defence in depth on the only step the public can see.

dist.schedule.cancel.title: Cancel Scheduled Publication
dist.schedule.cancel.summary: Compensation for dist.schedule.enqueue. Removes a queued item before its slot. The cheapest possible rollback, and the reason scheduling is preferred over immediate publication whenever the brief allows it.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

dist.schedule.enqueue.title: Schedule / Queue Publication
dist.schedule.enqueue.summary: Holds a ready PublishRequest until its slot, respecting per-channel rate limits and per-tenant pacing. Without this, a campaign that produces twelve posts publishes twelve posts in ninety seconds and burns the account.

dist.unpublish.blog.title: Unpublish Blog Post
dist.unpublish.blog.summary: Compensation for dist.publish.blog. Reverts to draft rather than deleting: a deleted URL that was indexed produces a 404 that outlives the mistake.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

dist.unpublish.linkedin.title: Unpublish LinkedIn Post
dist.unpublish.linkedin.summary: Compensation for dist.publish.linkedin. Deletes the post and records the reversal against the original trace, so a rolled-back campaign reads as one story in the ledger rather than two unrelated events.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

intake.audio.transcribe.title: Transcribe Audio
intake.audio.transcribe.summary: Voice note or audio file in, text out. Nothing else. The original screenshot fused download+transcribe+routing into the trigger workflow; splitting it means every future intake channel (WhatsApp, Slack huddle, phone call, meeting recorder) reuses this untouched.

intake.clarification.request.title: Ask a Clarifying Question
intake.clarification.request.summary: When the brief is too thin to act on, the system asks rather than guesses. Costs one message; a wrong guess costs a full production run and a human's trust in the system.

intake.message.normalize.title: Normalise Inbound Message
intake.message.normalize.summary: Any inbound shape (Telegram update, Slack event, email, web form, CRM webhook, schedule tick) collapses into one normalised message. This is the seam that makes the system omni-channel: a new intake channel is an adapter that produces this shape, and nothing downstream changes.

learn.playbook.revert.title: Revert Playbook Change
learn.playbook.revert.summary: Compensation for learn.playbook.update. Every accepted profile change is versioned, so reverting is restoring a version — not reconstructing what the profile used to say from memory.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

learn.playbook.update.title: Update Playbook from Results
learn.playbook.update.summary: The learning step. Proposes adjustments to channel weights, angle preferences and reuse bias from decisive results — and PROPOSES is the operative word: profile changes are versioned and require approval, because an autonomous system that silently rewrites its own strategy cannot be reasoned about.

measure.creative.score.title: Score Creative
measure.creative.score.summary: Turns raw per-channel metrics into one normalised 0-1 score comparable across channels and verticals, with a confidence weight for sample size. A score without confidence causes the system to chase noise, which is worse than not scoring at all.

measure.metrics.collect.title: Collect Channel Metrics
measure.metrics.collect.summary: Pulls per-post metrics back from each channel and writes them onto the ASSET, not just a report. That write-back is what closes the loop: tomorrow's asset search can filter on what actually worked.

media.audio.vo.generate.title: Generate Voiceover
media.audio.vo.generate.summary: Script to narration, with the voice characteristics taken from the vertical profile rather than hard-coded. Returns a durable audio asset plus per-line timings, which is what makes caption sync and beat alignment possible downstream.

media.captions.generate.title: Generate Captions
media.captions.generate.summary: Burned-in caption cues from voiceover timings or a transcript. Not decoration: most short-form video is watched with sound off, and every major platform ranks accessible content higher.

media.image.edit.title: Edit Image
media.image.edit.summary: Variant, inpaint, background swap, before/after pairing and brand-overlay composition on an existing asset. Editing an asset that already passed brand and rights review is materially cheaper and safer than generating a fresh one.

media.image.generate.title: Generate Image
media.image.generate.summary: One prompt in, one durable asset out. Handles provider fallback, base64-to-binary conversion and immediate promotion to durable storage — provider URLs expire, and an asset that expires mid-campaign is an outage nobody catches until a post is already live.

media.image.search.title: Search Asset Library (DAM)
media.image.search.summary: Semantic + structured search over everything the tenant has ever produced, filtered by rights and performance. The screenshots had this as a single 'Search Images' tool; promoted here to a first-class terminal because reuse-before-generate is the largest cost lever in the estate.

media.video.clip.generate.title: Generate Video Clip
media.video.clip.generate.summary: One beat, one clip. Submits an async job and POLLS to completion with a bounded budget. The original workflow used a fixed 90-second Wait node, which is wrong in both directions — it stalls fast jobs and silently truncates slow ones. Polling with a deadline fixes both.

media.video.render.title: Render Video
media.video.render.summary: Clips + voiceover + captions + brand furniture composed into a finished cut. Everything about the LOOK comes from the timeline template resolved per vertical; this workflow only knows how to assemble and poll.

media.video.render.before_after.title: Render Video — Before / After Proof
media.video.render.before_after.summary: Bound by local services. A wipe between two frames shot from the same position, with a locked evidence guarantee: the renderer refuses a pair whose frames were not flagged as real captures.

media.video.render.explainer_wide.title: Render Video — Explainer Wide
media.video.render.explainer_wide.summary: Bound by B2B software, industrial and home goods long-form. Slower cuts, lower-third captions, room for on-screen annotation, logo bug persistent.

media.video.render.ugc_vertical.title: Render Video — UGC Vertical
media.video.render.ugc_vertical.summary: Bound by e-commerce and any 9:16 slot. Hard cuts, oversized captions in the safe area, product held high in frame, offer end-card. A different FILM, not a different pipeline.

ops.budget.check.title: Budget & Policy Guard
ops.budget.check.summary: Called before every billable step. Returns allow / downgrade / deny. Centralising this is what lets a tenant cap be enforced across forty workflows without forty copies of the same arithmetic.

ops.budget.release.title: Release Budget Reservation
ops.budget.release.summary: Compensation for ops.budget.check. Releases a reservation when the work it was reserved for did not happen. Without this, failed runs slowly starve a tenant of budget it never actually spent.

observability.slo: 99.9% — a compensation that fails leaves the system inconsistent, which is worse than the original failure

plan.brief.synthesize.title: Synthesise Canonical Brief
plan.brief.synthesize.summary: The hinge of the whole system. Free-form human intent plus the vertical profile in, a validated Brief out. Everything downstream reads the Brief and never the original message — which is exactly why one content factory can serve a plumber and a SaaS without branching.

plan.campaign.compose.title: Compose Campaign Plan
plan.campaign.compose.summary: Brief in, an executable DAG of capability TAGS out — plus a cost estimate before a cent is spent. Selects from the vertical's declared plays rather than inventing a pipeline, which is what keeps an autonomous planner inside a shape operators have agreed to.

prompt.image.compose.title: Compose Image Prompts
prompt.image.compose.summary: Brief + vertical creative grammar in, structured image prompts out. Deliberately separate from generation: prompts are cheap to review, iterate and cache, while generations are not. The original screenshots coupled these two — splitting them is where most of the cost saving in this system lives.

prompt.image.compose.field_proof.title: Compose Image Prompts — Field & Proof of Work
prompt.image.compose.field_proof.summary: Bound by local services and industrial. There is no product shot: the proof is the work, the site and the person who did it. Polish actively reduces credibility here.

prompt.image.compose.lifestyle_room.title: Compose Image Prompts — Room & Interior
prompt.image.compose.lifestyle_room.summary: Bound by home_goods. Interiors fail on spatial logic long before they fail on style: wrong scale, impossible geometry and inconsistent light kill a frame that is otherwise beautiful.

prompt.image.compose.product_studio.title: Compose Image Prompts — Product Studio
prompt.image.compose.product_studio.summary: Specialisation bound by e-commerce and home-goods profiles. A product must be unmistakable, correctly proportioned and the right colour; everything else is negotiable. Fifteen lines of override, not a forked workflow.

prompt.image.compose.ui_abstract.title: Compose Image Prompts — Abstract / Conceptual
prompt.image.compose.ui_abstract.summary: Bound by B2B software and professional services. The product is invisible, so the image carries a concept. Legibility at thumbnail size beats detail every time.

research.product.fetch.title: Fetch Product / Offer Data
research.product.fetch.summary: Pulls first-party facts — catalogue attributes, spec sheets, reviews, CRM notes, usage data — from whatever system holds them. First-party data beats a model's recollection every time, and in regulated verticals it is the only acceptable source.

research.web.search.title: Web Research
research.web.search.summary: Bounded external research with source capture. Returns findings WITH urls so downstream copy can cite rather than assert — the single cheapest defence against a confident, wrong, published claim.

understand.intent.classify.title: Classify Intent
understand.intent.classify.summary: Cheap, fast, structured classification of an inbound message. Deliberately a nano-tier call: this runs on every message, and paying frontier prices to decide 'is this a question or a campaign' is how an estate's model bill quietly triples.

verify.brand.score.title: Brand Consistency Score
verify.brand.score.summary: Scores copy and imagery against the tenant's brand config before anything is rendered or posted. Catching a wrong palette here costs a cent; catching it after a render costs the render, and after a post costs the brand.

verify.compliance.screen.title: Compliance Screen
verify.compliance.screen.summary: Deterministic lexicon and pattern rules first, a model only for what a list cannot judge. A `block` finding is terminal: no downstream unit may proceed, and the run parks for a human with the finding attached.

verify.compliance.screen.strict.title: Compliance Screen — Strict
verify.compliance.screen.strict.summary: Bound by regulated verticals. Escalates the judgement model, treats every `warn` as a hold, and requires a named human reviewer role. Same pipeline, stricter thresholds — the difference between regulated and unregulated is configuration, not a second codebase.

verify.rights.check.title: Rights & Licensing Check
verify.rights.check.summary: Verifies every asset bound for distribution has a known, unexpired licence covering the intended usage scope. Purely deterministic — no model judges a licence.

sub.content.title: Content Factory
sub.content.summary: Brief in, channel-shaped copy out for every slot in the brief. Produces long-form once and shards it into channel-native short-form, which is why one research pass can feed a blog, five LinkedIn posts and an email without re-researching or contradicting itself.

sub.distribution.title: Distribution & Scheduling
sub.distribution.summary: Takes cleared creative and gets it out, one channel-neutral PublishRequest per slot, routed to the right adapter and paced by the queue. Adding a channel to the entire estate is one adapter plus one registry entry.

sub.governance.title: Brand & Compliance Governance
sub.governance.summary: The gate every publish-bound item passes through. Runs the cheap deterministic checks first, escalates only what needs judgement, and decides — from policy, not from the caller's optimism — whether a human sees this before the public does.

observability.slo: 100% of publish-bound items pass through this subsystem

sub.intake.title: Intake & Understanding
sub.intake.summary: Turns anything a human or a system sends into a validated Brief. Owns modality handling, PII redaction, intent classification and the clarification loop. Everything after this point in the estate reads a Brief and never a raw message.

observability.slo: 98% of inbound messages reach a Brief or a clarification within 60s

sub.measurement.title: Measurement & Learning
sub.measurement.summary: Closes the loop. Collects metrics, normalises them across channels, scores creative against the vertical's own benchmarks, and proposes — never silently applies — profile adjustments. Without this the system is a content printer; with it, it compounds.

sub.motion.title: Motion Factory
sub.motion.summary: The second screenshot, decomposed. Script to finished video: beats, keyframes, clips, voiceover, captions and render — every stage independently retryable, independently costed, and degradable to a still when a clip fails.

sub.visual.title: Visual Factory
sub.visual.summary: Brief in, reviewed imagery out. Owns the reuse-before-generate decision, prompt composition (routed per vertical), generation with fallback, and brand scoring before anything expensive happens downstream.

sys.gateway.title: Omni-channel Gateway
sys.gateway.summary: Every way work enters the system, in one place: a human messaging a bot, a webhook from a CRM or e-commerce platform, a schedule, or a direct API call. Its only jobs are to authenticate the source, mint a correctly-scoped Envelope, and hand off. It contains no marketing logic at all — that separation is why adding an intake channel never risks a production pipeline.

sys.orchestrator.title: Campaign Orchestrator
sys.orchestrator.summary: The loop: understand, plan, execute, verify, distribute, measure. It knows about capability TAGS and subsystems; it knows nothing about providers, platforms or verticals. Every branch it takes is a recorded decision, and every step it runs is late-bound through the router — which is what lets the same orchestrator run a plumber's job-of-the-week and an enterprise product launch without modification.

observability.slo: 95% of runs reach a terminal state (published, parked or declined) within their deadline
